title: Bitcoin governance seen as key variable in quantum-computing response
summary: German crypto asset manager DDA (Deutsche Digital Assets) said Bitcoin’s governance structure is one reason advances in quantum computing could pose a threat to the network. DDA said financial institutions such as JPMorgan could shift to quantum-resistant cryptography through board approval and budget execution alone, while Bitcoin would require consensus among participants worldwide. DDA added decentralized networks may adopt quantum-resistant cryptography more slowly than traditional financial institutions, and said this reflects not so much a weakness in Bitcoin as a need to take its governance process seriously.

title: BTC enters undervalued zone, but lacks capitulation and upside momentum
summary: Bitcoin has entered an undervalued zone, but the capitulation typically seen at cycle bottoms has yet to emerge, on-chain analyst Axel Adler Jr said on X.Adler said the MVRV Z-score, a metric used to assess oversold and overbought conditions, fell to 0.42, around four times lower than its historical average of 1.7, but remained above zero. BTC’s seven-day realized profit and loss turned positive from negative, indicating on-chain selling pressure has eased. He said the market has entered a stabilization phase while undervalued, but clear bottom signals and the demand needed to drive a fresh upswing are still lacking.

title: LDP lawmaker seeks to ease Japan’s 2x crypto leverage cap
summary: Seiji Kihara, a lawmaker from Japan’s Liberal Democratic Party, said Japan’s two-times leverage limit on cryptocurrency trading is overly restrictive and pledged to pursue regulatory easing, Nikkei reported. Speaking at a financial summit in Tokyo, Kihara said sufficient liquidity and a functioning price mechanism are essential for the healthy development of the crypto market, adding that deregulation is an unavoidable trend.Kihara currently leads the LDP’s Next-Generation AI and On-Chain Finance Project Team, which is pushing regulatory changes aimed at improving market liquidity and attracting more cryptocurrency capital to Japan, according to the report.

title: Coinbase CEO says crypto’s importance will grow in the AI era
summary: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said "AI has become a megatrend" but that does not diminish the value of cryptocurrency. In a post on X, Armstrong said crypto is general-purpose infrastructure like electricity or the internet, adding it is not competing with AI but instead supports it. Armstrong also said AI agents cannot open bank accounts or wait for wire transfers, so they need cryptocurrency as real-time programmable money. As AI agents take on tasks such as holding funds, making payments, trading, providing investment advice and raising capital, Armstrong said crypto’s role will grow further.
